ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.33 Ryde voucher to the rider (RydeTAXI metered-distance overcharge for the unexempted 09:24–09:30 segment); no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles that there is exactly one off-route segment, F3 (09:24–09:30, 3.78 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.71 km, +3.07 km, up to 688 m off route) [F3], so RD-1's shortest-and-most-direct obligation is engaged and only RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 could excuse it [RD-1]. RD-4 fails: no traffic incident is recorded near the route [F13], and the only speed bands are band 5 (40–49 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12], outside the band 1–2 congestion range RD-4(b) contemplates, with fair weather [F14]; speed-band evidence alone does not exempt anyway [RD-4]. RD-5 fails: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9] and contains only the rider's 09:04 pick-up message [F7] and the driver's 09:05 "2 min away" [F8] — neither names a road, an area or a stop, and both precede the 09:24 segment by nearly twenty minutes without any route agreement, so no rider message sent before 09:24:50 agrees to the segment [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that "the GPS rerouted" him [F10] is not rider consent and, as a statement, cannot outrank the gps and chat records [RD-5]. RD-3(a) also fails: no rider message named a place for the segment [F7][F8], and no stop was measured in it [F3]. The segment therefore counts as an unexempted deviation [RD-1].

Because the trip is metered RydeTAXI, extra distance flows into the meter [RD-2]. The rate is the fare record's own distance fare ÷ distance km: $34.42 ÷ 24.41 km = $1.4101/km [F6][F4]. The refundable amount is the unexempted segment's own extra_km: 3.07 km × $1.4101/km = $4.3290 → $4.33 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual between the segment extra_km and the billed excess (3.20 km − 3.07 km = 0.13 km, ~$0.18) is mileage not attributed to any segment and is expressly not refunded under RD-2 [F1][F3][F4]. Both advocates converge on this figure.

RD-6 is not met: the profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so no account flag follows, and profiles cannot be used to decide the case in any event [RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F7][F8] and the driver's statement [F10] — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; this is a fare-and-route dispute only [SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured [F3], the rate is in the fare record [F4][F6], the chat record is complete and timestamped [F9], and the RD-4 incident screen is closed [F13], so every element the ruling needs is settled.

segment_findings.reason: The complete, fully timestamped chat record [F9] holds only the rider's 09:04 pick-up message naming no road or place [F7] and the driver's 09:05 message [F8]; both precede the 09:24–09:30 segment, so no rider message before the segment agrees to it, and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted him [F10] is not rider consent [RD-5]. No rider-named stop appears either, and none was measured in the segment [F3][RD-3]. With no traffic incident [F13] and only band 5 speeds [F11][F12], RD-4 does not excuse it; the segment's 3.07 extra_km is refundable [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The RD-4 conclusion is accepted, not rejected — no incident on the replaced stretch [F13] and band 5 speeds [F11][F12] are outside band 1–2, so no reasonable-cause exemption attaches [RD-4]. Recorded here only because the rider's C4 is framed as a rebuttal of a defence the driver's advocate ultimately concedes; it changes no amount.

The driver's original $4.51 measure (3.20 km × $1.4101) is not the RD-2 measure: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's own extra_km, 3.07 km × $1.4101 = $4.33, leaving the ~0.13 km of fare-excess outside any segment unrefunded [F3][F4][F1][RD-2]. The driver's advocate withdrew this position in rebuttal, and the ruling adopts $4.33.

The suggestion that the outcome be limited to the meter refund 'not an account flag' is adopted in result — RD-6's route_disputes_upheld_90d is 0 [F16], so no flag_account is issued [RD-6] — but the rider's profile [F15] is not usable to decide the fare, and the deviation's size does not shrink the remedy: the full 3.07 extra_km is refundable [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Accepted as to the RD-1 finding on the record (one segment, 3.07 km, no exemption) [F3][F1][RD-1], but its premise that the trip-level +3.2 km is refundable is wrong: RD-2 refunds only segment-attributed extra_km, so $4.51 becomes $4.33 [F4][RD-2]. Claim id retained for the trace's accounting of conceded points.
Accepted: F16 shows route disputes upheld in 90 days = 0, so RD-6's repeated-breach threshold is not met and the rider expressly seeks no flag_account [F16][RD-6]. No account action is taken.
